task.question: What was the location of the train collision in Spain on January 20, 2026?
task.evidence: 20 January – A Rodalies de Catalunya train collides with a retaining wall that had fallen on the track in Gelida, killing the driver and injuring 37 passengers.

answer:
The location of the train collision in Spain on January 20, 2026, was in the municipality of Adamuz, in the province of Córdoba. 

FINAL: Adamuz, Córdoba

[2026 Adamuz rail disaster] On 18 January 2026, an Iryo high-speed train derailed in the municipality of Adamuz, in the province of Córdoba, Spain. A second train, Renfe Alvia 2384, crashed into it and was also derailed. The incident killed 46 people, including the Renfe train driver, and injured 292 others, 15 critically. The crash was Spain's worst railway disaster since the Santiago de Compostela derailment in 2013, and was the fourth deadliest railway accident in Spain until 10 months later, when at least 69 people died in the October 2026 Toledo train collision. A preliminary investigation by the Civil Guard found that a poor weld with an improper kit had caused rail breakage, and was compounded by poor data collection practices, inexperienced track inspectors, and overly relaxed programming of track circuit-connected alert systems. The line reopened for service on 17 February 2026 after a month of repairs and testing. | другие статьи: 2026 Toledo train collision, 2026 Spanish general election

On 18 January 2026, an Iryo high-speed train derailed in the municipality of Adamuz, in the province of Córdoba, Spain.
A second train, Renfe Alvia 2384, crashed into it and was also derailed.
The incident killed 46 people, including the Renfe train driver, and injured 292 others, 15 critically.
The crash was Spain's worst railway disaster since the Santiago de Compostela derailment in 2013, and was the fourth deadliest railway accident in Spain until 10 months later, when at least 69 people died in the October 2026 Toledo train collision.
A preliminary investigation by the Civil Guard found that a poor weld with an improper kit had caused rail breakage, and was compounded by poor data collection practices, inexperienced track inspectors, and overly relaxed programming of track circuit-connected alert systems.
The line reopened for service on 17 February 2026 after a month of repairs and testing.

The Iryo train, travelling northbound with 289 passengers and 5 crew members on board, left its scheduled stop at Córdoba–Julio Anguita station at approximately 19:39.
At 19:43, passing through the municipality of Adamuz, its three rear carriages derailed and invaded the opposite parallel (southbound) track, while the front of the train continued on the original (northbound) track.
The Renfe train, travelling southbound on the parallel track with 184 people on board, collided with the derailed Iryo train about 20 seconds later and also derailed.
The Renfe train sustained more severe damage
